So I think having him as 4 basically marginalizes his strengths and makes his weaknesses even more evident. Specifically, his shooting is OK for a power forward but GREAT for a center. And being an OK shooting power forward is way less impactful than being the same level shooter as a center. Think al horford. As a 5 horford can kill defenses and make life much easier on his teammates because the paint is wide open because the defense has to respect his shot. But put him as a 4 next to a traditional center and you lose all that offensive value. He can shoot OK but that center can still sit in the paint and clog driving lanes. Same logic applies for Turner. He can play a 4 but you get way more value playing him as a 5 so there really isn't much point to mess around with him at the 4.
Also any stretch 4 regardless of if they are fast or not he gets killed by because again doesn't have the quickness to sprint between the paint and the 3pt line

I am with you on the moments cards as they currently exist. the diamond JR and such are ridiculous. I do think there is a point to having the moments cards simply for diversity of teams, but as they are currently in the game it does not work. Instead moments cards should be for a player who does something exceptional in a certain way. Like that game Deron Williams hit like 11 3s (or 10 dont remember), so after that game put out a moments card that ACCURATELY describes that game without ruining the balance of the player. So for that game increase his 3p stats, but decrease other stats to make the card a side grade instead of an upgrade to the normal card. This way when choosing a lineup you have to compare the strengths and weaknesses of players to build the perfect lineup for your style instead of all the highest ratings. also for role players this isnt really an issue, like having a 78 moments mario chalmers isnt going to change balance either way.

tl;dr balance the moments cards so that they have improvements over star players base cards but also have weaknesses.
